findings.title: Boolean outer-worker liveness erases the unknown state
findings.trigger: A recovery caller observes a launch-bound outer worker with no claimed PID yet, or a live PID whose recorded start identity cannot be validated on the current platform.
findings.impact: status and cancel receive the same false value for both proven stopped and unprovable state, allowing recovery code to clean up evidence and roots before the worker boundary is safe.
findings.evidence: The function returns only alive true or false. pid null returns false at line 508; a missing current identity also returns false at line 514. Callers cannot distinguish either case from processAlive(pid) returning false at line 509.
findings.suggestion: Return one conservative state value from this shared function and update every caller once: alive, stopped, or unknown. Preserve raw PID liveness only for the explicitly retained unbound cross-platform P2; never convert a bound but unavailable identity into stopped.

findings.title: Worker lock readback does not verify the persisted start identity
findings.trigger: The claimed run.lock is replaced or altered between its atomic write and readback while retaining the same delegation id, launch id, spec digest, and PID but dropping or changing worker_start_identity.
findings.impact: claimWorkerLock returns true and launches the Host without proving that the recovery lock durably binds the exact worker start identity, recreating the identity gap that Repair 2 is intended to close.
findings.evidence: claimed includes worker_start_identity at line 278, but the persisted comparison checks only delegation_id, launch_id, spec_digest, and pid; it never compares the persisted identity to claimed.worker_start_identity.
findings.suggestion: Include worker_start_identity in the exact readback equality check, comparing both type and value or exact null. Refuse Host launch on any missing, changed, malformed, or unexpectedly supported identity.

positive_observations: The candidate centralizes lock and receipt conflict checks in one recovery-facts reader instead of duplicating guards at each caller.
The worker refuses Host launch when the lock cannot be claimed and retains an outcome_unknown lock and fence for explicit recovery.
limitations: This review did not expand into Host-created sessions or a portable replacement for Linux procfs start identity; those remain P2 scope.
